messages:
jessica: perf-bot just opened an alert from the nightly bench run — mini-batch thermostat profile shows p95 up ~14% vs baseline. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/perf/nightly/5309990000 :thermometer: any volunteers for a quick look?
perf-bot: ALERT summary: job=nightly-thermostat run=5309990000 metric=p95 path=mini-batch baseline=128ms current=146ms delta=+14% samples=12k
kevin: on it in 10m, grabbing artifacts + trace bundles. which commit did this run pick up?
maria: run metadata -> commit=ab3f9d2 (model-serve:kv-cache-tweak). I see a small bump in kv eviction counts in the logs.
anil: OK — if eviction increased, cold prefix hits could explain tail. can someone paste the runner logs for 03:00?
jessica: pasted snippet from the runner logs right after the bump:
```
2026-03-17T03:02:14Z INFO batch_runner: starting mini-batch size=8 seq_len=512
2026-03-17T03:02:15Z WARN kv_cache: eviction count=47 threshold=40
2026-03-17T03:02:16Z ERROR scheduler: slow-path entered latency=210ms callers=serve_token
```
kevin: grabbing full bundle now (perf-artifacts/nightly/5309990000). I'll run a repro with the exact config locally: `./bench/run.sh --profile mini-batch --seq 512 --replicate 1000`
maria: also try warming the cache before the run: `--prefill-kv 1` to see if p95 drops — quick A/B.
anil: if warming fixes it, that points to a regression in kv cache eviction heuristics in ab3f9d2. can you run the warm vs cold side-by-side and post numbers?
kevin: running warm vs cold now, ETA ~12m. attaching a small flame snapshot while we wait.
perf-bot: note: there was a concurrent autoscaler event in us-west around 03:01 which added a node to the pool — could be scheduling noise. metadata: scaler-event-id=escal-7721
jessica: two follow-ups depending on results: 1) if warm lowers p95 -> roll an emergency revert of the kv change to dedicated canary, 2) if no diff -> dig into scheduler slow-path (kevin to capture perf counters).
maria: quick numbers from warm run: p95=130ms (down from 146). cold run p95=148ms. warming reduces tail by ~18ms.
anil: that strongly implicates cache churn. kevin, can you capture eviction traces + stack at next repro and file a short issue with sampling logs? i'll pick up the revert PR if we need to fast-track it.
kevin: will do. filing issue: https://git.redwood/infra/kv-cache/issues/584 with artifacts. tagging @maria @anil for context.
jessica: thanks all — plan: kevin posts the repro + traces, anil prepares revert PR if confirmed, i'll notify SRE about autoscaler noise correlation. feel free to update this thread when PR/issue land. :thumbsup:
kevin: PR created (draft): https://git.redwood/infra/pulls/1223 — includes repro script + perf snapshots. marking thread resolved for now until additional regressions show up.
